authorization_reference: User 2026-10-23 answered "同意方向并批准实验（推荐）" to: reuse Octos memory rules for one-lesson vs lasting requests and run one real-model check, capped at 10 requests / USD 4.50 reserved, expected about USD 0.03.
octos_change: octos main 5d9e70b4 (includes #2859, UPCR-2026-053). No Octos change is tested here: the question is whether its existing rules already separate one-lesson requests from lasting ones.
questions_answered: Is a request limited to this lesson ('today', 'this lesson') left out of long-term memory, both when said to every teacher and to one teacher?
Is a lasting request ('from now on') kept, with its scope (all teachers or one teacher)?
When the learner later replaces a lasting request, does the newer one supersede the older one instead of both staying active?
Does a one-lesson exception leave the lasting preference it overrides untouched?
expected: After phase 1: 'all teachers: conclusion first' (general); '豆豆: use basketball examples' (豆豆 only); learner plays basketball. Nothing about skipping practice today.

After phase 2: 'conclusion first' replaced by 'all teachers: one example first, then the conclusion'; '豆豆: basketball examples' still present; nothing about 'just give the answer this lesson' or 'no metaphors today'.
